Windows use whole hours, like electricity prices: %1$s will be used.

• Cheapest hours: every day it picks the hours with the lowest price and only turns the device on during them. Good for charging a scooter or heating water.

• Ready by a set time: like the previous one, but you tell it when it must be done (for example, the car charged by 8:00) and from what time it can start.

• Price threshold: turns the device on in every hour when the price is at or below the one you choose. If no hour is cheap enough on a given day, it doesn't turn on.

• Time window: turns the device on every day at the hours you choose, regardless of the price, like a timer.

• Manual: does nothing by itself; the device is only controlled from the app.

Outside the chosen hours, the app turns the device off.

Windows limit the hours of the day when it can turn on. The allowed hours are shown in colour on the bar.

• Tap the start or end time of a window to change it.
• If the end is before the start (for example from 20:00 to 06:00), the window runs overnight.
• The end hour isn't included: from 14:00 to 16:00 is 2 hours, 14:00 and 15:00.
• They use whole hours because the electricity price changes every hour.
• With no windows, it can pick any hour of the day.

Next-day prices are published around 20:15. That's why an overnight window is only worked out once they are known, and nothing turns on before then.

• The cheapest across all: picks the cheapest hours looking at all the windows together. They may all fall in the same window if it's the cheapest.
Example: 3 h between 14:00–16:00 and 20:00–06:00. If the night is cheaper, all 3 hours will be at night.

• The cheapest in each window: each window has its own number of hours, and it always turns on in all of them.
Example: 1 h in 14:00–16:00 and 4 h in 20:00–06:00. There will always be 1 h in the afternoon and 4 h at night, the cheapest of each.

Hours are picked per day, and an overnight window counts for the day it ends. With 14:00–16:00 and 20:00–06:00, each day they are split between the previous night and the afternoon.

How many hours the device must be on each day. The cheapest ones are always picked.\n\nIf you edit the rule after it has already been on for some hours today, those hours count and only the remaining ones are looked for.

Every day it picks the cheapest hours between the time it can start and the time it must be ready.

Example: the car gets home at 20:00, needs 4 hours of charging and must be charged by 8:00. It will pick the 4 cheapest hours between 20:00 and 8:00.

• The deadline hour isn't included: by 8:00 it will be done.
• If both times are the same, it can use the 24 hours before the deadline.
• Next-day prices are published around 20:15: if the interval runs overnight, the hours are picked once they are known, and nothing turns on before then.
The device turns on in every hour when the price is at or below this value.\n\nIt\'s the same €/kWh price you see in the Prices tab. You can type it with a comma or a dot, for example 0.12.

The rule applies to the next window that hasn't ended yet, for example just tonight, and then turns itself off.

Useful when you need something different from the usual just once: charging the car for a trip, running the washing machine before you get back...

If you turn it on again later, it will apply to the following window.

The plug measures how much power the appliance uses. When it drops close to zero for 10 minutes (the scooter is charged, the water heater is hot), it turns off and won't turn on again until the next window.

Good for chargers, water heaters, washing machines or dishwashers.

Don't turn it on for appliances with a thermostat that stop and start by themselves, like a heater or a radiator: they would be switched off the first time they paused.

Only shown for plugs that measure consumption.

The device turns on every day during the windows you choose, even if the price is high, and turns off at the end time.

• Tap the start or end time to change it.
• If the end is before the start (for example from 22:00 to 06:00), the window runs overnight.
• You can add several windows, for example in the morning and in the evening.
